notes: Site: Umbraco-headless SPA (sostrenegrene.com), Denmark market at /da (culture=da-DK, market=DK). Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no WAF/block; robots.txt Allow: / with no Claude-specific disallow. Checked: main /da/produkter top-category tiles (no 'Outlet' tile), footer nav 'Shop' link group, and the full /da/sitemap.xml (37k lines) grepped for outlet/udsalg/restlager/restparti/kup/sidste-chance -- zero hits for 'outlet', 'udsalg' (sale) or 'restlager'/'restparti' (remaining stock) anywhere on the site; the site does NOT use those words. Instead found two genuinely distinct clearance-style pages via footer nav ('Shop' link group), both under the site's own crossCategory taxonomy: FOUND #1: 'Fortrinlige kup' (literally 'Excellent bargains/finds' -- Danish idiom for a great deal on used/leftover stock), URL /da/landing/fortrinlige-kup, categoryId=2010, crossCategory='campaign'. Its own on-page copy: 'Soestrene har vaeret paa loftet for at rydde ud og har fundet et vaeld af fine ting og sager frem fra gemmerne. De har derfor samlet dette udvalg saerligt til de sparsomme, der oensker at goere et fortrinligt kup' = 'The sisters have been up in the attic clearing out and found a wealth of fine things put away in storage. They have put together this selection especially for the frugal who want to make an excellent bargain' -- explicit permanent clear-out/discontinued-stock framing (attic clean-out, items 'put away'), matching the CLEARANCE test (site's own copy describes permanent markdown/discontinued stock, not a temporary % -off campaign). Queried via GET /umbraco/api/catalog/search?categoryId=2010: total=68, reproduced 11/13 repeat calls (fresh sessions + delayed re-checks, cookie-session-pinned and unpinned) after an initial transient total=83 seen on the very first 2 calls -- treating 68 as the settled/reproducible value per the prior Home-Decor pass's documented backend-replica-desync behavior on this same site (noted then for a different category), and NOTING the transient 83 in this evidence rather than silently discarding it. Sample product names confirm real leftover/discontinued furniture & home items (Sidebord/side table, Puf/pouf, Skammel/stool, Skrivebord/desk). FOUND #2: 'Sidste chance' (Last Chance -- one of the brief's own listed Clearance target terms), URL /da/landing/sidste-chance, own H1 'Sidste chance', copy: 'Oplev soestrenes udvalg af populaere favoritter med kun faa tilbage paa lager, og sikr Deres favoritter, foer det er for sent' = 'Discover the sisters' selection of popular favorites with only a few left in stock, and secure your favorites before it's too late' -- a genuine dedicated last-chance/low-stock landing page. HOWEVER captured via Playwright network trace that its actual product feed is /umbraco/api/recommendation/ProductsFromUmbracoBlock?...recommendationType=Personal&limitToLowStockProducts=true&numberOfRecommendations=72 -- a PERSONALIZED, session/algorithm-driven recommendation feed (returns a plain array, no 'total' field, capped at a requested max of 72, not a fixed catalog total) -- the site itself does not report an exact count for this listing anywhere, so qty is null per Rule 2 rather than guessed from the 72 request-cap or the 144 DOM links (=72 products x 2 links each) observed in one rendering. These two are genuinely different listings (different URLs, different product sets/mechanisms -- one a fixed categoryId catalog listing, the other a personalized low-stock feed) so both are kept as separate rows, not merged. No general '% off / Sale / Udsalg' promotional page was found anywhere on the site to weigh against these (so no Sale-vs-Clearance ambiguity to resolve) -- the site simply has no such generic promo page in its taxonomy.
